drills.title: Round to two decimals
drills.prompt: Arrange the lines so the program prints the total rounded to 2 decimals. The two declarations can go in either order. Two lines do not belong.
drills.explain: Math.round(x * 100) / 100.0 rounds to 2 decimals. The 100.0 matters: dividing by the int 100 would throw the decimals away again. Variables are declared before they are used.

drills.title: Operators, casts and Math
drills.prompt: Fill the blanks so the program prints the goal output.
drills.explain: int / int drops the decimals (3). % is the remainder (1). Casting to int cuts 3.99 down to 3 without rounding. Math.ceil rounds up and returns a double (5.0).

drills.title: Numbers surprise
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
drills.explain: int / int stays an int (3); one double makes it 3.5. A cast cuts decimals (3). Math.round rounds .5 up (3 and -2). Decimals are stored in binary so 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3. An int that passes its ceiling wraps around to a negative number.

drills.title: The int division trap
drills.prompt: The BMI of 70 kg and 175 cm should be about 22.9, but the program prints something else. Click the faulty line and choose the fix.
drills.explain: heightCm / 100 is int divided by int, so Java drops the .75 and gets 1 before storing it in a double. Make one side a double (100.0). Casting after the division is too late.

drills.title: Review the AI's box planner
drills.prompt: An AI assistant wrote this planner. It compiles and runs, but tick the real problems (there are two).

issues.text: boxes is 3.0, not 3.5 (or 4 boxes needed), because items / perBox is an int division
issues.why: Both operands are int, so the decimals are dropped before the result goes into a double. Use items / (double) perBox, or Math.ceil for whole boxes.

issues.text: views goes past the int ceiling and wraps around to a negative number
issues.why: Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1 overflows silently to -2147483648. Use a long when a counter can pass about 2 billion.

non_issues.text: share loses its decimals because people is an int
non_issues.why: total is a double, so total / people is a double division.

non_issues.text: phone must be an int because the number has no decimals
non_issues.why: 9876543210 is too big for an int. long (with the L suffix) is the right choice.

non_issues.text: Joining a double and a text with + is a compile error
non_issues.why: + with a text converts the other side to text. It compiles and works.

drills.explain: Silent numeric bugs are the classic weakness of generated code: the program compiles and prints something plausible. Check every / between ints and every counter that can grow large.
